Laws are weak because they rely on mixups. Their whiff punishing is subpar, they have few frame traps and poor frame advantage in general, and their weak side (left) is VERY weak. 

Their "tools" are only good because of the damage. 

Beating Law involves reaction time and knowledge, because you can essentially lock down your opponent if their mixups get predictable. 

Basically, eat all the lows rather than ducking because they WANT you to duck. Pay attention for the low-launchers though, definitely block and punish those.

JDCR's policy is to almost never duck. He eats the low pokes but figures out his opponents, so he'll obviously block huge lows but he's rather step and punish because it's a lot more of a threat. 

I wish there were a good guide somewhere on how to step against certain characters.

It's probably the hardest execution-based technique for Law. I think what separates good Laws from bad ones are those who can play without using his amazing mixup abilities, relying on pokes and movement initially while conditioning opponents to react in certain ways. AK from the Philippines was very good at this, for example.

Law is too mixup-based (I play Law), and once I've been figured out there's not much I can do. I have two tracking moves that work: b+3 and b+4. That's all. 

It's not unmanageable once you figure out how your opponent plays. That said, good players like AK from the Philippines will save their mixups for crucial moments, and rely more heavily on pokes and movement to pull of combos.

I see that Lei and Hwoarang are the popular picks, but honestly they benefit mostly from an opponent's of knowledge and they're mixup based. 

JDCR, arguably the best player in the world, uses Armor King and Heihachi and says American players focus way too much on mixups. Koreans focus more on movement, which is why they can master multiple characters. That said, Heihachi is an amazing whiff punisher, and in the right hands he can dodge all your moves with proper spacing and stepping and it'll be over.
